facts.text: Vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) and mixed reality use a real complete machine or a major physical subsystem with its controllers and actuators.
facts.quote: **What is real:** the complete machine or a major physical subsystem with its controllers and actuators.

facts.text: Vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) requires a real machine on an enclosed safe test area, or a dynamometer, wheel-hub or actuation bench; a virtual environment; and virtual targets injected into the sensor stream or ECU, or physical sensor stimulation.
facts.quote: a real machine on an enclosed safe test area, or a dynamometer, wheel-hub or actuation bench; a virtual environment; virtual targets injected into the sensor stream or ECU, or physical sensor stimulation

facts.text: Vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) requires feedback of the physical machine's state into the virtual world so that subsequent stimuli are regenerated.
facts.quote: feedback of the physical machine's state into the virtual world so that subsequent stimuli are regenerated.

facts.text: ASAM's requirements-based VIL methodology describes over-the-air stimulation of largely unmodified vehicles, including the full physical sensor and software chain; the passage labels this expert opinion based on on-road evidence.
facts.quote: ASAM's requirements-based VIL methodology describes over-the-air stimulation of largely unmodified vehicles that includes the full physical sensor and software chain.

facts.text: Vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) can prove real braking dynamics, actuator and controller delays, latency and the operator interface without endangering people or real targets.
facts.quote: **Proves:** real braking dynamics, real actuator and controller delays, real latency and the real operator interface, without endangering people or real targets.

facts.text: Vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) bridges simulation and field testing.
facts.quote: It is the bridge between simulation and field.

facts.text: Vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) cannot prove sensor perception of injected objects unless the sensors are stimulated over the air.
facts.quote: **Cannot prove:** sensor perception of the injected objects unless they are stimulated over the air.

facts.text: A vehicle-in-the-loop bench may not reproduce soft soil, grades, tire or track sinkage, articulated or tracked dynamics, payload behaviour, vibration, dust or weather.
facts.quote: A bench may not reproduce soft soil, grades, tire or track sinkage, articulated or tracked dynamics, payload behaviour, vibration or dust and weather

facts.text: The size of heavy machines makes vehicle-in-the-loop facilities difficult.
facts.quote: the size of heavy machines makes facilities difficult.

facts.text: Radar target simulation for vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) has been demonstrated on roads.
facts.quote: radar target simulation for VIL has been demonstrated on roads.

facts.text: The 2024 survey reports VIL limitations in road and testbench fidelity, physical signal generation, multi-target radar simulation, multi-camera systems and especially lidar stimulation.
facts.quote: The 2024 survey reports limitations in road and testbench fidelity, physical signal generation, multi-target radar simulation, multi-camera systems and especially lidar stimulation

facts.text: The 2024 survey did not identify a full-scale VIL platform ready for comprehensive industrial testing of automated vehicles at the time of publication; this is on-road evidence.
facts.quote: did not identify a full-scale VIL platform ready for comprehensive industrial testing of automated vehicles at the time of publication.

facts.text: Off-road vehicle-in-the-loop evaluations were not found.
facts.quote: Off-road VIL evaluations, and comprehensive VIL on production-scale haul trucks, wheel loaders, dozers or excavators: not found.

facts.text: Comprehensive vehicle-in-the-loop testing on production-scale haul trucks, wheel loaders, dozers or excavators was not found.
